episodes.title: AI Pipelines, Creatine, and Goodbyes
episodes.description: Steven shows the fully automated video workflow he built with Claude, which turns one MOV file into transcripts, translations, captioned shorts, and Substack drafts. He also tests five cameras, talks about Gary Vee's one-topic-per-account approach and his first days on creatine, and remembers two people who died, urging listeners to reach out to old friends.

episodes.title: Back at the Lectern: Recordings, Speeches and AI
episodes.description: Back in Beijing after the National Day holiday, Steven talks about new classroom rules: students must record their group discussions and give two-minute talks instead of reading from their phones. He also covers the privacy costs of AI agents, his four-terminal editing setup, a possible October stock market drop and Facebook Muse.

episodes.title: A Smoggy Jog and the Decision to Make Fewer Videos
episodes.titleZh: 雾霾慢跑与少拍视频的决定
episodes.description: Back in Beijing the day before returning to work, Steven runs through heavy smog, talks about heavy squats, his doubts about creatine and his caffeine rules, and takes an honest look at his weak video numbers and Xiaohongshu shadow bans. He also covers progress on his AI-powered language-learning project and three Chinese stocks he's watching after the National Day holiday.

episodes.title: Rhinitis, Supplements and a Passport Video Post-Mortem
episodes.titleZh: 鼻炎、补剂与护照视频复盘
episodes.description: Steven recovers from rhinitis and looks at how his "Is a passport really necessary?" video did across six platforms, where it earned 19 cents in total. He also explains why he's sticking with his online backup plan, corrects Xiaomi founder Lei Jun's name, and walks through his new supplement routine of red ginseng, pea protein and creatine.

episodes.title: A Golden Week Sunday Spent Wrestling with Local AI
episodes.description: During the National Day holiday, Steven talks about microphone trouble, blue Beijing skies, a run and end-of-range squats. He then spends a Sunday building a mostly local AI workflow that might replace paid tools like Descript, and weighs its power against the privacy risks.

episodes.title: Pricey Tacos, Easy Bonds
episodes.description: Steven visits Beijing's Juicy Taco Festival, where the tacos cost too much but the old friends made the trip worth it, and he talks about Beijing rents, foreign workers forced out of China by age rules, and editing his US trip videos. He ends with a plain-language explanation of why bond prices fall when yields rise.

episodes.title: National Day Special: 5,000 Years of China in Brief
episodes.titleZh: 国庆特辑：五千年中国速览
episodes.description: On National Day, Steven gives a personal tour of what "5,000 years of Chinese history" means, running from the Shang dynasty to China as the world's factory. Along the way he covers cities worth visiting, why "Hong Kong" and "Xianggang" sound so different, his favourite foods, and his girlfriend's claim that Marco Polo stole pizza from China.

episodes.title: Office Hours and China's Blueberries
episodes.description: Jet-lagged and waiting on a takeout delivery, Steven talks about getting back to the gym, meeting his first classes at his new university, and a surprise in his contract: his office hours are monitored and averaged. He ends with a Wall Street Journal story on how China learned to grow blueberries and why they still cost so much there.

episodes.title: Back in Beijing, Jet-Lagged
episodes.description: Jet-lagged and just off a 12-hour flight from Vancouver, Steven describes the trip back to Beijing: crammed luggage, a customs check, a stubborn headache, his new teaching job and his YouTube plans. He ends by asking whether he really wants to stay in China for the long term.

episodes.title: Last Night in Canada: Ready for Beijing?
episodes.titleZh: 加拿大最后一夜：准备好回北京了吗？
episodes.description: On his last night in Canada, Steven says goodbye to family and friends, lays out his three-day trip back to Beijing, and admits his plan to move his work online this year didn't work out. He also talks about his cymbal album, splitting his language blog between Substack and YouTube, and why convenience, not love, is what keeps him in China.

episodes.title: The Trip Home That Started With Half a Bottle of Water
episodes.description: Steven flies home from Toronto to Winnipeg and runs into one problem after another: a security fight over half a bottle of water, an $18 airport beer, a forced bag check that ended in a broken zipper, and a hurried plan to get back to his job in Beijing. He also explains the difference between travel and medical insurance, and tells how he climbed a borrowed ladder to clear out his mom's eavestroughs.

episodes.title: Walking Across the Bridge, Farewell to America
episodes.description: Recording at Toronto Pearson Airport, Steven wraps up his 2026 summer road trip across America. He describes walking across the new Gordie Howe International Bridge into Canada and being searched by customs, looks back on Detroit and the Rust Belt, and explains why he still recommends visiting the US.

episodes.title: From an Airport Bench to Lake Erie
episodes.description: Steven records from a Cleveland-area truck stop after a sleepless night on a Buffalo airport bench, a pricey walk-in car rental, and a day exploring Buffalo, dipping his feet in Lake Erie, and reaching Cleveland. He reflects on the costs of travel in America, his improvised travel style, and whether to stay for the air show or press on to Detroit.

episodes.title: Buffalo: Wings, Strangers, and a Closed Door
episodes.titleZh: 布法罗：鸡翅、陌生人与闭门羹
episodes.description: Steven records outside a Buffalo tavern and recounts a night in a traveling salesman's hotel room, a free manuscript museum, Buffalo wings at Gabriel's Gate, and being turned away from a charity house. He weighs pricey options for leaving town and asks whether anyone can really travel the U.S. this way, and he also meets a bartender who is learning Chinese.
